report:
**Yes — the evidence strongly supports that denosumab (Prolia) reduces the risk of vertebral fractures in osteoporosis.**

The primary evidence comes from the **FREEDOM trial** (Fracture Reduction Evaluation of Denosumab in Osteoporosis Every 6 Months), published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* in 2009. This phase 3 randomized controlled trial enrolled 7,868 postmenopausal women aged 60–90 with osteoporosis (T-scores between −2.5 and −4.0). Participants received denosumab 60 mg or placebo subcutaneously every six months for 36 months. Denosumab produced a **68% relative risk reduction in new vertebral fractures** compared to placebo, along with significant reductions in hip (40%) and nonvertebral (20%) fractures. This benefit was consistent across all pre-specified subgroups (age, BMI, baseline T-score, prior fracture status).

The FDA approved Prolia in 2010 primarily on the basis of the FREEDOM trial. The FDA label states: "In postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, Prolia reduces the incidence of vertebral, nonvertebral, and hip fractures."

A **10-year extension study** published in *The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology* (2017) showed that fracture incidence rates remained low over a decade of continuous treatment, similar to the original three-year denosumab group and lower than projected placebo rates.

**Important caveat:** Discontinuing denosumab without transitioning to another antiresorptive agent is associated with a rebound increase in bone resorption and a heightened risk of **multiple vertebral fractures** within months of stopping. Delayed doses (>4 months late) also raise vertebral fracture risk. This means the fracture-protective benefit depends on consistent, ongoing treatment.

**Sources:**
- FREEDOM trial (NEJM 2009): https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa0809493
- 10-year extension (Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2017): https://www.thelancet.com/journals/landia/article/PIIS2213-8587(17)30138-9/fulltext
- FDA Prolia label: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/125320s186correctedlbl.pdf
- Denosumab 10 years later review (PMC): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8799550/
